expectedBehavior: A valid reviewed response should pass on the first call; an invalid response may receive one bounded repair; every started or uncertain call must become durable terminal evidence and must never rerun.
observedBehavior: S13 high required a costly repair, S14 medium was first-response valid on the same BDD request with different semantics, and S15 high plus medium Activity-ready attempts both entered repair but lost exact validation diagnostics. Current fake paths prove mechanics, not the real provider trigger.

hypotheses.statement: A prompt, projected strict schema, or deterministic validator mismatch causes some real first responses to fail.
disconfirmingEvidence: s14 medium used the same prompt/schema/validator and was first-response valid
provider-free valid responses pass the same validator
hypotheses.smallestProof: Capture repeated exact validation code/path events and reproduce the dominant event provider-free without changing accepted meaning.

hypotheses.statement: Repair resends the complete projection and makes any first-response defect expensive.
supportingEvidence: S13 repair repeated 15114 input tokens and cost 349535.310 ms
current service embeds the complete projection plus diagnostics in repair input
disconfirmingEvidence: This explains cost after repair entry, not why the first response was invalid.
hypotheses.smallestProof: Identify the trigger first; compare full versus targeted repair only after exact repeated diagnostics exist.

hypotheses.statement: High reasoning effort increases first-response invalidity or latency for some readiness inputs.
supportingEvidence: S13 high repaired while S14 medium was valid on the same BDD input
disconfirmingEvidence: S15 Activity-ready high and medium both entered repair
hypotheses.smallestProof: Run the same frozen human-reviewed case under one selected control first; only a later separately audited comparison may attribute control effects.

hypotheses.statement: Host evidence/request authoring leaves responsibilities that readiness cannot resolve reliably.
supportingEvidence: Readiness owns omission and selection-quality review after host authors JSON 1 and JSON 2
disconfirmingEvidence: The observed failure is response validation before policy, not a proven authority gap
hypotheses.smallestProof: Show the same validation failure persists after a reviewed complete request or trace it to missing host authority.

hypotheses.statement: The old S15 runner failed to persist completed-invalid/provider-failure observations and validation diagnostics.
supportingEvidence: S15 stopped after four calls with only checkpoint role/state counts
offline regression fix now terminalizes those paths
disconfirmingEvidence: The runner defect is fixed and does not explain provider response invalidity.
hypotheses.smallestProof: Use the new fake-proven diagnosis lifecycle for any new identity; never resume S15.

hypotheses.statement: No current evidence uniquely identifies the first-response validation trigger or safely selects a correction level.
supportingEvidence: S13/S15 exact validation diagnostics are absent
no human-reviewed readiness diagnosis case exists
several hypotheses remain compatible with observations
hypotheses.smallestProof: Obtain two genuine reviews plus adjudication for the visible bridge case, then freeze/audit one new readiness-only maximum-two-call package with durable diagnostics.

recommendation.reason: The decisive real validation trigger and genuine human-reviewed case authority are both absent.
recommendation.decisiveTradeoff: Targeted repair could reduce the proven cost amplifier but may optimize the wrong defect or hide semantic invalidity before the trigger is known.
